transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time, because it's probably not a huge deal, but... I came in because I've been feeling, well, just sort of wound up lately? Almost all day long. 

It's kind of hard to explain, but it feels like my body is just... bracing for something. Even when I’m just sitting at my computer working, or trying to relax after dinner. I just can't seem to shake that tense feeling. Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I made an appointment for that.
How long have you been feeling this tense, wound-up sensation?

Well, I guess... um, it's been about thirteen months? I hope I didn't wait too long to come in. I really thought it would just pass on its own, you know? 

It started right around the time my sister—she lives down in Arecibo—started needing a lot more help from our family. I mean, I'm happy to help her, of course, and I really shouldn't complain because she's the one who actually needs the support. I feel a little silly even mentioning it, honestly. But I think that's when this tense feeling kind of settled in for me. Is it okay that I waited this long to see someone about it?
Is this tense feeling always present, or does it get worse in certain situations?

Um, well... I wouldn't say it's *always* present, at least not in a way that stops me from doing what I need to do. I mean, I can still work and everything. It's just sort of... humming in the background most of the time? 

I guess it does flare up a little bit when I have to figure out the logistics for my sister, or if I feel like I'm falling behind at work because I was on the phone with her doctors. But really, it's not terrible. I'm probably making it sound worse than it is. I just notice that my shoulders are up by my ears a lot. Does that sound like the kind of thing you usually see, or am I just not handling stress very well?
Do you feel more tense or wound up in social situations, like when you're around other people?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think so? Being around other people doesn't really bother me. I actually like being around my coworkers and my friends. 

If anything, I think sometimes talking to other people kind of distracts me from that tense feeling, you know? Unless I'm talking to them about my sister's situation, I guess. But just normal social things... no, I don't feel more wound up then. I hope that's a helpful answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain tasks or activities because of this tense feeling?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I avoid things. I mean, I'm still getting all my work done, and I'm always showing up for my family and for church. I would really hate to let anyone down! 

But... um... I guess I have noticed that it takes me a little longer to finish my reports lately. I just find myself double-checking things a lot more than I used to, just to be absolutely sure I didn't make a mistake. And, well, I feel awful even admitting this, but I've had to apologize a couple of times recently for sounding a bit short with people I care about. I really don't mean to be snappy! I just get so wrapped up in trying to keep everything on track. 

I'm still managing everything, though, I promise. I just have to work a little harder at it right now. Is it normal to get a little irritable and slow down like that when you're stressed? I hope I'm answering your question the right way.
Do you find yourself having recurring thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?

Um, well... I guess I do have some thoughts that kind of stick around. But I think that's just because I want to make sure I'm taking care of everything properly, you know? 

Sometimes I'll be at work, and I'll tell myself, "Daniela, enough, focus on this report." But then... I don't know, one small thought about my sister's appointments or something turns into five more. And before I know it, I've spent half an hour checking messages or just sort of replaying what could go wrong. 

I feel so silly admitting that, because I know I should just be able to push it out of my mind and focus. I'm really trying to get better at it, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of thing you were asking about.
Have you experienced any physical symptoms like headaches or stomach problems alongside this tense feeling?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I've had anything like that. My stomach is fine, and I don't really get headaches. I try to take good care of myself, you know, eating right and drinking enough water so I don't get run down. 

I mean, maybe I've felt a little tired at the end of the day, but that's just normal when you're busy, right? I wouldn't call it a physical problem or anything. I hope that's okay? I just haven't really noticed any big issues like that.
Do you often feel like you're fidgeting or have an urge to move around when you're sitting still?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm fidgeting, exactly. I mean, I sit at my computer all day for work, so I'm pretty used to being still. I try to maintain good posture and everything. 

But... I guess I do feel a bit... wound up? Like, almost all day long. It's actually kind of why I came in to see you. It's just this feeling like my body is constantly bracing for something to happen. Even when I'm just sitting at my desk, or, you know, trying to relax on the couch after dinner. 

I don't want to make it sound worse than it is! I'm still getting everything done. It's just this tight feeling that doesn't really go away. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Has this tense, wound-up feeling been causing you a lot of distress or interfering with your daily life in a significant way?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say it's causing a *lot* of distress. I don't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything! I'm still getting all my work done, and I'm always there for my family and for church activities. I really make sure of that. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, maybe it is affecting things just a little bit? Like, it seems to take me longer to finish my reports at work lately because I feel like I have to double-check everything more than I used to. Just to be absolutely sure it's right, you know? And... well, I have had to apologize a couple of times recently for sounding a bit short with people I really care about. Which isn't like me at all, I promise! I try so hard to be patient. 

It's just that tight feeling makes it hard to focus sometimes. I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than I should be. Does that sound like what you were asking about?
Do you feel like you're repeatedly thinking about certain things over and over, even when you try to stop?

Oh, well... I try very hard not to. I really do try to keep my mind productive and on track. But, um... I suppose sometimes my thoughts do get a little bit stuck? It's silly, really, I probably shouldn't even mention it. 

I'll be at my desk and I’ll tell myself, ‘Daniela, enough, just focus on this report.’ But then... I don't know, one small thought just kind of turns into five more? And before I even realize it, I’ve spent maybe half an hour just checking my messages or replaying everything that could possibly go wrong. 

I always catch myself eventually and get right back to work, though! I promise I'm not just sitting there wasting time all day. I always get my tasks done. Is that... is that normal to do sometimes? I really hope it doesn't make me sound too scatterbrained.
Do you feel like these thoughts about your sister's situation are popping into your mind without you intentionally thinking about them?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say they just pop in out of nowhere. I'm usually just... trying to think through how to help her, you know? 

I really try to keep my mind focused on what I'm doing, especially at work. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting there letting my mind wander all over the place when I'm supposed to be working. It's more just that... when I do think about her, which is natural because I care about her so much, it just kind of... spirals a little bit, like I mentioned before. But I'm the one who starts thinking about it, usually. 

I try very hard to stay in control of my thoughts. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question the right way.
Do you ever find yourself thinking about your sister's situation when you're not intentionally trying to think about it?

Oh, um... I think maybe we just talked about that a little bit? I'm sorry if I wasn't clear before! I really try my best to give you the right answers. 

But, um, no, I wouldn't say they just happen on their own when I'm not trying to think about it. I'm usually deciding to think about her because I want to figure out how to be helpful. I don't just lose control of my thoughts like that, I promise! I always try to stay very focused on whatever I'm supposed to be doing. 

I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Do you ever have thoughts about your sister's situation that feel like they're intruding into your mind, even when you're trying to think about something else?

Oh dear, I'm so sorry, I feel like I must be doing a terrible job explaining myself since you're having to ask again! I really want to give you the right answer, I promise. 

But, um... no, I really wouldn't use the word intruding. They don't force their way in when I'm trying to focus on my computer work or anything like that. I don't have thoughts that I can't push away, I assure you. It's truly just me deciding to sit down and figure out how to help her... even if I end up spending a little too much time on it once I start. 

Is that... does that help clarify things? I really hope I'm not being difficult! I just want to make sure I'm being completely honest with you.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop thinking about your sister's situation even when you want to think about something else?

Oh, um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I try really hard to stop. I'll tell myself, "Daniela, enough, you need to focus on this report," because I really do want to do a good job at work. I don't want you to think I'm just slacking off. 

But sometimes... I guess once I've decided to think about it, it's hard to put the brakes on? Like, one small thought about how she's doing turns into five more thoughts, and then... well, before I know it, maybe I've spent half an hour checking my messages to see if she texted, or just replaying all the things that could go wrong. 

It's not that I'm completely out of control, I just... I care so much, and it's hard to turn that off once I start trying to fix it. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for... I'm really trying to explain it right.
Do you feel like thinking about your sister's situation is causing you a lot of emotional pain or discomfort?

Oh, um... pain? I wouldn't say pain, exactly. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or being dramatic about it! I know there are people dealing with much worse things. 

I mean, it's not always the most comfortable feeling, because of course I worry about her. But it's just because I care, you know? It's just a normal amount of sisterly concern, really. I wouldn't call it painful or... or unbearable or anything like that. I manage it just fine, I promise! I don't let it completely ruin my day. 

I hope that's okay to say? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm falling apart over it, because I'm really trying my best to handle everything well.
Do you ever find yourself thinking about your sister's situation when you're in the middle of doing something else and hadn't intentionally meant to think about it?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I don't think so? Like I said before, I really try to stay focused on my work. I wouldn't want to be the kind of person who just zones out and lets their mind wander when they're supposed to be doing something important. 

If I'm thinking about her, it's usually because I've sat down and decided to check in or, you know, figure out a plan. It doesn't just pop up out of nowhere while I'm typing an email or something. I'm usually very good at keeping things separate! 

I really hope I'm answering this right... I know you've asked about this a few different ways, and I'm so sorry if my answers aren't what you're looking for. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information!
Do you feel like you can control when you think about your sister's situation, or does it happen without you deciding to think about it?

Oh, I... I know we were just talking about this, and I really hope I'm not confusing things or... or sounding inconsistent. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. 

I guess... well, like I mentioned before, I do try so hard to control it. I'll literally tell myself, "Daniela, enough, you need to focus on this report right now." Because I really do want to be a good employee and stay on task. But... sometimes, once a little thought starts, it just sort of... rolls? 

Like, I might just have one tiny thought about how she's doing, and then that turns into five more thoughts, and... well, before I even realize what's happening, I've spent half an hour checking my messages or just replaying all the things that could go wrong. 

So I guess... maybe it is a little hard to control once it starts? I don't mean to sound like I'm completely helpless or anything! I just... I get so caught up in caring for her. Is that... is that normal? I hope that makes sense and answers your question better.
Do you ever have thoughts about your sister that you didn't intend to think about and can't easily dismiss?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I know I just said they can snowball a little bit sometimes, but I really wouldn't say I can't dismiss them! If I absolutely have to, I can always push those thoughts away and get back to my computer. 

I don't want to give you the impression that my mind is just... out of my control, or that I'm sitting there completely taken over by things I don't want to think about. I'm actually very diligent about snapping out of it when I need to. I always manage to pull myself together! 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm contradicting myself from a minute ago? I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound worse than it really is, and I definitely don't want you to think I'm losing my grip on things. Am I making sense?
Do you feel like your worries about your sister and other things are excessive and difficult to control?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't use the word "excessive," really. I think I just care a lot about the people in my life, and I want to make sure everything is taken care of. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around panicking all day! 

But... I suppose my mind does tend to jump around a bit. Like, I'll be thinking about my sister down in Arecibo, and then I'll suddenly wonder if I forgot to send an important email at the office, and then I'll start thinking about my husband driving home in traffic, or what I need to do for church this weekend, or if the bills are all sorted... 

I guess I just like to be prepared? Sometimes I catch myself trying to solve problems that haven't even happened yet. But I really try to keep it all under wraps so it doesn't bother anyone else. Is it... is it bad that my mind does that? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by trying to stay on top of everything.
Do you feel like you can easily stop worrying about your sister and other things when you want to?

Oh, gosh, I feel like I'm repeating myself, and I'm so sorry if I'm not being clear... I really just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. 

When I want to stop... well, like I was mentioning earlier about my work, I really do try to just put my foot down with myself. I'll say, "Daniela, that's enough, you need to focus on this report." I put a lot of effort into being disciplined! But... easily? I suppose... maybe it isn't always easy. Because, like I said before, I'll have that one little thought, and then it just turns into five more, and before I even realize what's happening, a whole half hour has gone by with me just checking my messages or imagining everything that could go wrong with my sister or the house. 

I always try my best to pull myself out of it, though! I don't want you to think I just sit there and let it happen without a fight. I really do try. Am I explaining that okay? I hope I'm not being too repetitive or frustrating you.
